content: Omeprazole is a medication that can cause your immune system to attack other cells or organs in your body, a condition known as an autoimmune reaction. If you experience new or worsening joint pain or develop a rash on your arms or cheeks, notify your healthcare provider immediately. Omeprazole may lead to vitamin B-12 deficiency by reducing the absorption of this essential nutrient. This risk is higher if you take omeprazole for an extended period, such as three years or longer. Symptoms of vitamin B-12 deficiency include a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling and numbness in your hands or feet. If you experience any of these symptoms, stop taking omeprazole and contact your healthcare provider. Omeprazole can also cause low magnesium levels, a condition known as hypomagnesemia, which can be serious. Low magnesium levels may result in seizures or heart rhythm problems. Individuals who take omeprazole for a long time or use other medications that lower magnesium levels are at higher risk. Symptoms of hypomagnesemia include changes in heart rate or rhythm (such as a fast or skipping heartbeat), dizziness, muscle spasms, or seizures. If you experience any of these symptoms, stop taking omeprazole and consult your healthcare provider. Long-term use of omeprazole may lead to bone loss and increase the risk of fractures, particularly in older adults or those taking high doses. If you are at risk, discuss this with your healthcare provider. Omeprazole can cause severe allergic reactions. If you experience symptoms such as difficulty breathing, wheezing, a racing heart, fever, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing, throat tightness, itching, skin rash, hives, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, lightheadedness, fainting, stomach cramps, or joint pain, stop taking the medication and seek emergency medical attention immediately. People allergic to omeprazole, Prilosec, Prilosec OTC, other proton pump inhibitors, or any ingredients in the specific product should not use omeprazole. Your pharmacist can provide a list of ingredients in the product. Omeprazole may interact with other medications. Before starting omeprazole, inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking. Specific medications that may interact with omeprazole include clopidogrel, cilostazol, citalopram, methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, certain antiretroviral medications (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir), St. John’s Wort, and rifampin. These interactions may alter the effectiveness of omeprazole or the other medications. Always consult your healthcare provider for guidance. Do not take omeprazole unless prescribed by a healthcare provider. Follow the prescribed dosage and instructions. Do not share omeprazole with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. Keep omeprazole out of reach of children. Do not chew, cut, or crush the medication. Take it before a meal. If you have difficulty swallowing the capsule, you may open it and sprinkle the contents on one tablespoon of applesauce, swallowing it immediately without mixing it with other foods. Omeprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn and may take 1 to 4 days to work fully. Before using omeprazole, inform your healthcare provider about your health conditions, including low blood potassium (hypokalemia), low blood magnesium (hypomagnesemia), low blood calcium (hypocalcemia), or liver problems. This information will help determine if omeprazole is appropriate for you. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your healthcare provider. It is not known if omeprazole affects pregnancy or harms an unborn baby. Omeprazole can pass into breast milk, so it should not be taken while breastfeeding. Store omeprazole at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C) and protect it from excessive heat or moisture. It can tolerate short-term exposure to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C), such as during transportation. Keep it in a cool, dry place. If you accidentally take too much omeprazole, seek medical help immediately by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take double or extra doses. Omeprazole is used to treat conditions caused by excessive stomach acid, such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), ulcers, erosive esophagitis, and Helicobacter pylori infections. It works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. It is available in various forms, including capsules, tablets, and powders for oral suspension. Common side effects of omeprazole include headache, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, gas, and, in children aged 1 to 16 years, infections in the nose or throat and fever. If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. Serious side effects, such as kidney problems, antibiotic-associated diarrhea, severe skin reactions (e.g., Stevens-Johnson Syndrome or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis), or a severe allergic reaction called DRESS, require immediate medical attention.
